audit_rule: A candidate may be HIGH only if the available Yale-derived primary pixels support a unique, physically defensible before->after reconstruction without inventing hidden strokes. Apparent correction morphology by itself is insufficient.
resolution_scope: Public Yale-derived digital imagery and frozen locator crops available during this audit; no multispectral, raking-light, microscope, or physical-manuscript examination was available.

candidates.reason: Localized superposed/darkened strokes are visible, but more than one lower-layer glyph history is compatible with the pixels; no unique pre-state can be recovered.
The central glyph is visibly abnormal/darkened, but the underlying state is obscured and published observers propose incompatible reconstructions. Primary pixels do not resolve a unique predecessor.
A discrete local stroke anomaly survives, but its temporal order and the unmodified glyph cannot be determined uniquely from the image.
The affected glyph is localized and partially legible, but overlapping strokes admit multiple before-states; selecting one would be post-hoc paleographic inference rather than visible reconstruction.
Dense dark overwrite destroys the lower-layer topology at available digital resolution; the pre-state is not recoverable.
Closely doubled vertical strokes are clearly visible, but a content-changing correction cannot be separated from reinforcement/retouching and no unique initial glyph is visible.
The candidate glyph is locally darkened, but the available primary image does not expose a unique overwritten predecessor or stroke chronology.
Strong darkening is visible, but page-level re-inking/retouching is a confound for this folio; a unique content correction and prior form cannot be established from pixels alone.
Superposed local strokes are visible but do not determine a unique pre-correction glyph or operation ordering.
The candidate is dominated by a dense dark loop/blob; the underlying form is not recoverable at available digital resolution.
Low-contrast strokes do not support a defensible stroke-order or before-state reconstruction.
Paired/darkened tall strokes are visible, but reinforcement versus content-changing addition and the initial glyph remain unresolved.

block_reason: After complete review of the preregistered candidate set using available Yale-derived primary digital imagery, zero events permit a unique HIGH-confidence before->after reconstruction; the frozen minimum is six independent events.
interpretation_boundary: BLOCKED means this particular confirmatory natural-experiment design lacks enough recoverable correction events in the available digital evidence. It does not show that the manuscript has no corrections, that its text is meaningless, or that no stronger imaging modality could recover earlier stroke states.
